summary: CLS regression verification after HomePage eager-import fix (iter385). Measured homepage CLS on mobile 390x780 and desktop 1440x900 using PerformanceObserver({type:'layout-shift', buffered:true}) installed via add_init_script BEFORE navigation. Load + 3s wait + scroll top-to-bottom in 400px steps @ 350ms. Both viewports pass the <0.1 target with a very wide margin. Hero H1 'Discover./Bid./Win.' renders immediately (no PageLoader flash). Fix confirmed working.

top_shifts.source: svg (footer language/logo area, y=726, no positional change — likely rasterization only)
div.absolute.w-1.h-1 particles repositioning (hero decorative particle animation)

desktop_1440x900.verdict: PASS (0.00427 << 0.1 target, 56x improvement from iter384 0.2418). All top shifts are tiny 4x4px decorative particle movements on desktop — these are intentional animations, not layout shifts of real content.

verification_checklist.blobs_particles_hidden_mobile: confirmed — mobile had only 1 shift entry vs desktop 16 (particles absent on mobile)

action_items: None — CLS fix is fully effective. Mobile CLS=0.00144, Desktop CLS=0.00427, both far below the 0.1 threshold.

OPTIONAL: The desktop particle animation contributes ~all remaining CLS (still trivially small). If ever needed, wrap particles in a transform-only animation or add contain:layout paint on the particle container so they don't register as layout shifts. Not required.
critical_code_review_comments: Reverting HomePage to eager import is the correct fix — homepage is the LCP-critical route so lazy-loading it forced a Suspense fallback swap that caused footer displacement. Other routes correctly remain lazy.
Consider using CSS transform (translate) instead of top/left for the .w-1.h-1 particle animations to eliminate the residual desktop shifts entirely (currently ~0.004 total, harmless).
